title: Masterpiece
text: You found the crayons. And a very large, very white wall.
Your parents left you alone for thirty seconds. The wall now has art on it.

outcomes.text: I drew a dinosaur eating the sun. Nobody appreciated it.
My parents framed a photo of the wall. They'll show it at my wedding.
Purple tastes like purple.
A parent's hand came out of nowhere and removed it. I have never forgotten the betrayal.
I covered both arms. It took four baths and my parents took photographs of every one.
It turned out not to wash off, and I went to a family gathering looking like that.

title: Bath time
text: It's bath time. You have other plans.
Someone is running a bath. You know what that means.

outcomes.text: The bathroom floor is a lake. I'm very proud.
I soaked the bathroom, the hallway and one very surprised cat. Bath time is shorter now, permanently.
I made it all the way to the front yard.
I slipped on the wet floor and bonked my head.
Rubber duck and I had a peaceful soak.
I behaved so well they let me stay in until my fingers went strange and wrinkled.

title: A new word
text: You learned a new word today. You won't stop saying it.
A grown-up said a word you'd never heard. You liked it.

outcomes.text: My new word was "no". I said it 400 times.
The word was one my dad said when he stubbed his toe. Grandma heard it.
I whispered it to the cat.
I forgot it entirely by dinner. Whatever it was, it is gone now.
I used it in completely the wrong places for a month and nobody had the heart to correct me.
Somebody corrected me in front of everyone and I did not say it again for a year.

title: A big dog
text: A dog the size of a pony {~walks up to|wanders up to|lumbers towards} your stroller {~outside {fx.shop}|on {fx.street}|in {fx.park}}.

outcomes.text: The dog licked my entire face. Best friends.
The dog knocked me over. I cried. The dog also cried, I think.
I screamed. The dog ran. So did the owner.
I screamed, and the dog thought it was a game. It licked my entire face while I kept screaming.
It took the biscuit with enormous gentleness and then sat down next to the stroller like a bodyguard.
It took the biscuit and my entire hand went in with it. No damage, enormous noise.

title: Daycare
text: It's your first day at daycare. {~Someone's crying, and it might be you.|The room smells of paint and orange squash.|Every tiny human here is looking at you.}
Someone dropped you off in a room full of other tiny humans, and there is a box of {~wooden blocks|crayons with no paper|a rocking horse with one ear}.

outcomes.text: I shared my blocks with a kid named {f.first}. Now we share everything.
I tried to share, but a kid bit me.
I cried for three hours. The teacher deserves a medal.
I cried for eleven minutes and then discovered the sand table. I did not think about home again.

choices.label: Sit in the corner and watch

outcomes.text: I watched everything for two days and then joined in as though I had been there all along.
I watched from the corner for the whole fortnight and they rang my parents about it.

title: Big kid potty
text: Your parents have been talking about "the big kid potty" all week.

outcomes.text: Success! There was a sticker chart. I got all the stickers.
There was an incident. We don't talk about the incident.
I refused on principle.
I refused, held out for six days, and then changed my mind entirely on my own terms.
I held out for a sticker chart and a specific biscuit. I got both. Early lessons in leverage.
I negotiated too long and the moment rather resolved itself on the hallway carpet.

title: The big slide
text: The big-kid slide at {fx.park} is SO tall. {~Everyone else is already at the top.|A boy at the bottom is watching you.|The ladder has more rungs than you've ever climbed.}

outcomes.text: Fastest anyone has ever gone. I have a bump to prove it.
I went head first, misjudged everything, and landed in the one patch of mud. Photographic evidence exists.
Wheeee. Again. Again. Again.
I went down normally, once, decided that was enough, and spent the rest of the afternoon watching.
A bigger kid yelled at me. I won.
A bigger kid yelled at me, an adult yelled at the bigger kid, and I stood there feeling enormous.

title: Sleepover
text: {f.first} invited you to a sleepover.
It's your first sleepover, at {f.first}'s house.

outcomes.text: We stayed up until 2 a.m. telling ghost stories. Worth it.
I got scared and called my mom to pick me up at midnight.
We froze {f.first}'s brother's underwear. Legends.
We got caught. Everyone went to bed at 9.
I fell asleep first. They drew on my face.
I fell asleep first and woke up before everyone, ate all the good cereal and watched cartoons alone. Ideal.

title: Lemonade stand
text: It's hot out. The perfect day for a lemonade stand.

outcomes.text: I made $18 and drank most of the profits.
One customer. It was my dad. He paid in hugs.
A man in a suit paid $5 and said I'll go far.
Zero customers. The market has spoken.

choices.label: Put a secret ingredient in it

outcomes.text: The secret ingredient was hot sauce. The reviews were intense.
The secret ingredient was too much sugar. We sold out in an hour and one customer came back for more.

title: The bully
text: {b.first} has been stealing your lunch every day.
{b.first}, the biggest kid in class, has decided you're the target this year.
{b.first} keeps tripping you in the hallway.

outcomes.text: I told {b.first} to back off, loudly, in front of everyone. It worked.
{b.first} gave me a black eye. But now everyone knows I don't back down.
{b.first} got detention for a week and left me alone.
The teacher said to "work it out". Great.
I made a joke about myself before {b.first} could. {b.first} laughed. We're sort of friends now.
It didn't work.
I kept my head down. It went on for months.
I kept my head down, and a kid I barely knew sat next to me every day until it stopped.

title: Science fair
text: The science fair is next week.
Your teacher announced the science fair. Everyone groaned.

outcomes.text: Classic. Participation ribbon.
I made it erupt all over the judges. First place for 'enthusiasm'.
My homemade solar oven cooked an actual egg. First place!
My robot caught fire. The fire alarm went off. Everyone went home early.
My dad built a working hovercraft. The judges knew. I knew. We all knew.
My dad took over and it collapsed on the table during judging. He apologised to me for a week.

title: Loose tooth
text: Your tooth has been wiggling for a week. {~You can't stop touching it with your tongue.|Your dad has offered to 'help' with a piece of string.|It's hanging by a thread during lunch at {fx.primary}.}

outcomes.text: I tied it to a door. It worked! The tooth fairy left $5.
I tied it to a door. The door won, but the tooth stayed.

choices.label: Wait for it to fall out

outcomes.text: It fell out in my sandwich. Tooth fairy paid extra for the trauma.
It fell out during class and I lost it in the carpet. No tooth, no payment, one very long negotiation.

choices.label: Stay up to catch the tooth fairy

outcomes.text: I saw my mom tiptoe in with a dollar. I pretended to be asleep forever.
I fell asleep at eleven and woke to a dollar. The mystery survived another year, which I now think was the point.

title: Field trip
text: Your class is going on a field trip to {trip}.
Field trip day! The bus is leaving for {trip}.

outcomes.text: I learned more than I expected. The gift shop was the best part.
I stuck with the group, got travel sick on the coach, and remember the journey far better than the museum.
I found a secret exhibit nobody else saw. Also, the teachers were looking for me for an hour.
I got lost. A security guard walked me back. Humiliating.

choices.label: Sit with your crush on the bus

outcomes.text: We shared headphones the whole way. Best day ever.
They moved seats. I'll never recover.

title: Class goldfish
text: It's your turn to take the class goldfish home for the weekend. {~He's called Gerald.|The teacher reminded you three times.|You've already named him something else.}

outcomes.text: Mr. Bubbles returned to class alive and possibly happier.
I took excellent care of it and it died anyway, on a Tuesday, for no reason I was ever given.
I'm convinced it learned to swim through a hoop. Nobody believes me.
It ignored every hoop and swam in the same slow circle for a fortnight. I learned something about expectations.
Mr. Bubbles was replaced by a slightly different Mr. Bubbles. My mom handled it.
Mr. Bubbles survived my neglect entirely. Some things are harder to kill than a seven-year-old assumes.

title: Recess
text: It's recess at {fx.primary}. {~The whole playground is yours.|Somebody has already claimed the good swing.|The football game has started without you.}
The bell rang for recess. {~Everyone ran.|The rain had stopped, which nobody believed.|The teacher on duty has a whistle and a grudge.}

outcomes.text: I was never 'it'. Undefeated.
I was 'it' the entire time. My legs hurt.
I traded a doubles card for a super-rare shiny. Business genius.
A fifth-grader scammed me out of my best card.
I finished a whole chapter book.
I read under a tree until a ball hit the book out of my hands. I read indoors after that.
We have a password and a treehouse. Adults may not enter.
The club lasted nine days and ended in a dispute over the password that has technically never been resolved.

title: Crash!
text: Your ball just went straight through the neighbor's window.

outcomes.text: The neighbor was so impressed I owned up that she gave me cookies. I still had to pay for the glass.
The neighbor yelled for ten minutes. My parents paid. I paid my parents.
Nobody saw. The guilt ate at me for weeks.
The neighbor has cameras. Very awkward dinner that night.
It worked. I'm a monster.
I blamed my sibling and nobody believed me for a second. Both of us were punished, and only one of us deserved it.

title: A hidden talent
text: Your teacher noticed you're unusually good at {skill}.
Turns out you have a knack for {skill}.

outcomes.text: I practiced every day. I'm better than most adults now.
I practised every day for two years and then, quite suddenly, could not stand the sight of it.
It's just for fun, and that's the point.
Keeping it a hobby meant nobody ever told me to stop, so I never did.
I never did anything with it. Sometimes I wonder.
I ignored it, and years later somebody I went to school with got famous doing exactly that thing.

title: Birthday party
text: It's your birthday! Your parents are throwing a party.
Happy birthday! There's a party, and a suspicious number of balloons.

outcomes.text: Twenty kids, one bouncy castle, zero survivors. Best party ever.
Only three kids came. My mom ate a lot of cake that week.
Pizza, a movie, and my best friends. Perfect.
Two of them cancelled that morning. The three who came made it the best one I had.
There was no pony. There was a man in a pony costume. Close enough.
There was, against every expectation, an actual pony. My parents never explained how.

title: Something under the bed
text: You're sure there's something under your bed. {~It breathes when the house is quiet.|It was there last night too.|The wardrobe door opened by itself.}

outcomes.text: Just socks. So many socks.
It was the dog. The dog was terrified too.
I slept between my parents. Everyone was kicked all night.
I got halfway down the hall, decided I was too old for this, and went back on my own.
I didn't sleep. But nothing got me.
I hid under the covers and fell asleep in about four minutes, which rather undermined the whole crisis.

title: Scouts
text: A scout troop is recruiting at school.

outcomes.text: I earned eleven badges, including one for knot tying and one for not crying on the campout.
I joined, hated every minute of the camping, and made one friend I still have.
Uniforms aren't my thing.
I said no, and spent the year listening to everyone else talk about it.

choices.label: Join, then quit after a month

outcomes.text: I joined, hated the shouting, quit cleanly, and nobody made it a thing. I learned I was allowed to leave.
I quit and my parents made it a thing for a very long time.

title: Spelling bee
text: You made it to the final round of the spelling bee. Your word: "{word}".

outcomes.text: Correct! I won the spelling bee!
One letter off. Runner-up.

choices.label: Ask for it in a sentence

outcomes.text: The sentence gave it away. Champion!
The sentence made it more confusing. I got it wrong.
I guessed, got it wrong, and was back in my seat inside nine seconds. The relief was enormous.
I guessed and it was somehow right, and then I had to keep going, which was the worst outcome available.

title: Money on the sidewalk
text: You found a $20 bill on the sidewalk.
There's money on the ground. Nobody's around.

outcomes.text: Candy. So much candy.
I kept it, spent it on sweets, and felt vaguely wrong about it for about a decade.
Nobody claimed it. The office let me keep it and gave me a certificate.
Someone claimed it. I got a thank-you and a warm feeling.
My future self thanks me.
I put it in savings and forgot about it entirely until somebody cleared out the account years later.

title: Chores
text: Your parents made a chore chart. Your name is on a LOT of it.
Your parents say it's time you pulled your weight around the house.

outcomes.text: I earned my allowance and my parents' respect.
I did them all, and the following week the list was longer. Nobody warned me that is how it works.
I got my allowance doubled for half the chores. Future CEO.
Negotiations failed. More chores.
I did them so badly they stopped asking. Genius or villain?
I did them badly once, was made to do them again properly, and learned an extremely boring lesson.

title: The new game
text: Everyone at school is playing a new game. You don't have it.
A new console came out. You need it. You NEED it.

outcomes.text: They caved. I haven't seen the sun since.
They said no. "Maybe for your birthday."
Six months of allowance later, it's mine. It feels earned.
Six months of saving, and by the time I had it, everyone had moved on to something else.
I basically moved in with my friend.
I played at a friend's house until their parents started calling me by name and setting a place at dinner.

title: Your first phone
text: Your parents are finally talking about getting you a {~phone|{era.phone}}. {~Everyone else in your class already has one.|There are a lot of rules attached, and one of them is about dinner.|You have been hinting for months.}

outcomes.text: I got a phone! Screen time rules apply. I broke them on day one.
I promised to be responsible and lost it within five weeks. There was not a second phone for a long time.
My parents were so shocked they got me one anyway.
I said I did not need one and genuinely did not, right up until every plan started being made without me.

choices.label: Ask for a rubbish one nobody wants

outcomes.text: I asked for the cheapest phone in the shop and got it immediately, and it did everything I needed for four years.
The cheap one broke in a fortnight and I was told that was the lesson.

title: Summer camp
text: Your parents signed you up for summer camp. Two whole weeks. {~The brochure shows a lake and far too many smiling children.|Your bag is packed, and there's a label in every sock.|You're not sure whether to be thrilled or terrified.}

outcomes.text: Canoeing, campfires, a camp crush and a talent show. Best summer ever.
I got poison ivy on day two. The rest was great.
They picked me up on day three. I kind of regret it.
I begged to go home, they said finish the week, and by Thursday I did not want to leave.
By the second week I knew every shortcut, every counsellor's name and where the good snacks were kept.
I tried to run the place and a counsellor had a quiet word about it that I still think about.

title: Snow day
text: School's canceled. {~It snowed overnight|The roads are closed|The whole of {fx.street} is white} and {~your mother is already looking for your other glove|somebody has a sledge|the sky is the colour of a blank page}.

outcomes.text: I built a snowman taller than my dad.
I built a snowman, went inside for twenty minutes, and came back to find it beheaded. I have suspects.
I pelted the neighborhood kids. Undefeated.
I took one to the face. Ice-filled. Rude.
The best kind of day off.
I stayed in bed and missed the only real snow of my entire childhood. It never came like that again.

title: Art contest
text: The town is holding a kids' art contest at {fx.library}. {~First prize is a box of 96 crayons.|Your teacher looked straight at you when she said it.|The judge is rumoured to be the mayor's wife.}

outcomes.text: My painting of a sad banana won first prize.
The judges "didn't get it".
My mom cried. I got an honorable mention.
I painted my family, got one of them badly wrong, and it became a joke that ran for fifteen years.
I copied something famous badly enough that it came out original, and it won a category nobody expected.
A judge recognised exactly what I had copied and said so, in front of people.

title: The party
text: There's a party at {host}'s house this weekend. Their parents are away.
Everyone is going to a party at an older kid's house on Saturday.

outcomes.text: I danced, I laughed, I got home just before curfew.
The cops showed up. I jumped a fence and ruined my jeans.
Someone posted a photo of me looking ridiculous. It's my profile picture now.
Nobody noticed. I'm a ghost.
My parents were waiting in the kitchen when I climbed back in.
I heard it was wild. I'll go next time.
I stayed home and nothing happened at the party either. Everyone said it was boring, and for once I believed them.

title: Breakout
text: A giant pimple appeared on your nose the morning of picture day.
Your face has betrayed you. There's a volcano on your chin.

outcomes.text: It made it worse. So much worse.
I popped it, it healed clean by the weekend, and I learned nothing that would help me later.
Nobody noticed. Probably.
I covered it up with something two shades off and that is what people actually noticed.
I named it Kevin and introduced it to everyone. People loved Kevin.
I tried to own it and the joke did not land. I went quiet for the rest of the afternoon.

title: The text
text: {c.first} just texted you out of nowhere: "hey"
You've had a crush on {c.first} for months. They just sat next to you.

outcomes.text: We talked for three hours. I didn't sleep.
I played it so cool they think I don't like them.
They feel the same. We're dating!
They said they "don't see me that way". I'm moving to Antarctica.
The meme landed. We've been sending memes daily ever since.
The meme did not land. They replied with a single full stop and I thought about it for two years.

title: First job
text: {fx.shop} down the street is hiring teens. {~The sign has been in the window for weeks.|A friend said the manager is a lunatic.|It pays just enough to matter.}

outcomes.text: I got the job! My uniform smells like fries forever.
They hired someone's cousin instead.
There's time to work later.
I enjoyed being young, and watched everyone with a job get their own money and their own plans.
I held out for something I actually wanted and got it two months later for more money.
I held out all summer and got nothing, and the burger place had already filled up.

title: Learner's permit
text: You're finally old enough to learn to drive. {~The form is three pages long.|Your dad is pretending to be calm about it.|Everyone you know has a story about their first lesson.}

outcomes.text: My parent gripped the dashboard the whole time. I'm improving.
I backed into the mailbox. It's gone.
My instructor was calm and patient. I'm ready for the test.
My instructor was a nervous man who gasped at roundabouts. I passed anyway, mostly out of spite.
I'll learn later. The bus is fine.
Not learning cost me two jobs before I worked out that it was costing me jobs.

title: Finals week
text: Finals are next week. You haven't studied.
A huge exam is coming. Your whole grade depends on it.

outcomes.text: Coffee, flashcards, panic. I aced it.
I fell asleep during the exam.
We quizzed each other for hours. Everyone passed.
The study group turned into three hours of talking and forty minutes of panic at the end.
I winged it. It went about as well as you'd think.
I winged it and somehow got a B. The universe is chaos.

title: New look
text: You want to reinvent yourself before the new school year.
You're sick of your look. Time for something new.

outcomes.text: Black everything. People look at me differently now.
Black everything. My mother asked, gently, whether I was alright, and I was, and I could not explain it.
Collared shirts and a new attitude. Teachers love me.
Collared shirts, and the people I actually liked started treating me like somebody else.
Hoodies and sneakers. Comfort is a lifestyle.
Hoodies and trainers, and I disappeared into the background so completely that it took a year to climb back out.
I'm fine as I am.
I stayed myself, which was harder that year than any of the alternatives, and worth it later.

title: Start a band
text: {f.first} wants to start a band in the garage. {~You've never played an instrument.|They already have a name and a logo and no songs.|The neighbours have not yet been told.}

outcomes.text: We call ourselves "Unpaid Parking Tickets". We have three songs. One is good.
We played one gig at a bowling alley. Four people clapped.
I booked our first show at a coffee shop. I'm basically a mogul.
I booked the show, four people came, and two of them were related to the drummer.
Garages are cold.
I passed, and they got good. I watched from the audience with a complicated feeling.

title: Caught
text: Your parents found something in your room they did not like.
Your parents found out you skipped school last week.

outcomes.text: They bought it. I feel terrible.
They did not buy it. Grounded for a month.
They were disappointed, but they appreciated the honesty.
I told the truth and it went far worse than lying would have. I have still not decided if it was right.
They made me stop hanging out with that friend. Oops.
I blamed a friend and they found out within a week. That friendship never really came back.

title: A trip abroad
text: Your school is organizing a trip abroad. It costs $2,000.

outcomes.text: I came back speaking a little of a new language and missing a place I'd never heard of.
I went, got homesick in the second week, and spent a fortnight being no use to anybody. I am still glad I went.
They paid. I owe them forever.
"Money doesn't grow on trees." I stayed home.
Maybe next year.
I skipped it, and heard about it from the ones who went for the next three years.

title: Caught on camera
text: Someone filmed you doing something stupid in the cafeteria.

outcomes.text: I became a school legend.
I leaned into it, and the joke outlived the moment by about eight months. I could not put it down.
They deleted it. It's already everywhere.
They deleted it, and because they deleted it, everyone assumed it was worse than it was.
My response video got more views than the original.
My response got twelve views. The original kept going.

title: Homecoming
text: It's homecoming week at {fx.secondary}. {~The whole school is buzzing.|Every corridor is covered in crepe paper.|There's a rumour about who's winning king.}
The homecoming game is Friday. {~The marching band has been practising since August.|Half of {fx.secondary} will be in face paint.|Someone has hung a banner across the gym.}

outcomes.text: We won in the last second. I lost my voice.
We lost by 40. Still fun.
I slow-danced with someone and my heart exploded.
I went to the dance, stood near the wall for two hours, and left before the last song.
Homecoming is overrated. Probably.
I stayed home and three people texted asking where I was. That was better than going.

title: College visit
text: Your parents want to take you to visit a college. {~It is four hours away and there will be a sandwich in the car.|The brochure is glossy; the dorm, the tour guide says, is 'cosy'.|You suspect they want you to be impressed.}

outcomes.text: I fell in love with the campus. Now I have to get in.
I visited, felt completely out of place, and understood something useful about what I actually wanted.
The tour guide showed us the 'best frat'. Mom was not amused.
The tour guide was earnest and clever and completely changed what I thought that place was.
My parents took it better than I expected.
My parents took it badly and we did not talk properly for most of a year.

title: Jury duty
text: A letter arrived: you've been summoned for jury duty.
You've been called for jury duty. Again.

outcomes.text: The trial was about a stolen goat. I'll never forget it.
The trial lasted six weeks. I know too much about tax fraud now.

choices.label: Try to get out of it

outcomes.text: I said I'm biased against everyone. They let me go.
The judge saw right through it. I served anyway.
They made me foreman. Twelve people, four days, one decision I still turn over.
They made me foreman and we could not agree at all. It collapsed, and it was nobody's fault and felt like mine.

title: The DMV
text: You have to renew your ID. The line at the office is {~out the door|longer than last time|stuck on a number that hasn't changed in an hour}. {~You brought a book.|You forgot one of the forms.|The woman in front of you has brought a folding chair.}

outcomes.text: Four hours. I aged a year. The photo is horrendous.
Four hours, and when I got to the front they told me I had brought the wrong form.
I met a fascinating stranger who used to be a trapeze artist.
I tried to make conversation and they put headphones on, slowly, while looking at me.
Security escorted me out. I still need my ID.
I complained loudly, and the entire queue quietly agreed with me. Something was actually fixed.

title: Flat tire
text: You got a flat tire {~on the highway|on {fx.street}|outside {fx.shop}}. {~It's raining.|It's exactly the wrong moment.|The spare is underneath everything you own.}
Your car shudders and pulls to the right. Flat tire. {~You don't remember how the jack works.|You had an appointment in twenty minutes.|Somebody slows to watch and keeps going.}

outcomes.text: I changed it in twenty minutes. I feel like an action hero.
I don't know how to change a tire. I do now, after three hours.
They came in an hour. $120.
Roadside took four hours and arrived after I had already worked out how to do it myself.
{f.first} came to the rescue with snacks.
{f.first} came, could not help either, and we sat on the verge talking until the van came.

title: Wrong number
text: You got a text from a wrong number. It's someone confessing their love.
A stranger keeps texting you thinking you're their sister.

outcomes.text: We texted for weeks before I confessed. Now we're pen pals.
I played along for two messages before it stopped being funny and started being sad.
They were mortified. We laughed about it.
I told them, and they were looking for somebody who had died. I did not know what to say.
Blocked.
I blocked them, and spent an oddly long time afterwards wondering who they had been trying to reach.

title: New year, new you
text: It's January. {~Everyone is joining {fx.gym}.|{fx.gym} has a queue at the door.|You can't find a parking space at {fx.gym}, and you haven't even signed up.} {~The membership is cheaper if you sign for a year.|The salesman has very white teeth.|You tell yourself you'll actually go.}
You made a New Year's resolution to get in shape.

outcomes.text: I went three times a week all year. I'm a different person.
I went twice in January. The membership still charges me.

choices.label: Buy the gear, skip the gym

outcomes.text: I look great in the outfits.
I bought the gear, wore it once, and it sat in a drawer as a monthly reminder for a year.
Honesty is healthy.
I made no resolutions, and then quietly started walking every evening without telling anyone.

title: The roommate
text: Your {~roommate|flatmate} keeps eating your food. {~There's a name on the milk, and it isn't theirs.|Yesterday it was the last of the cheese.|The fridge contains a note in the other person's handwriting.}

Your {~roommate|flatmate} has a new partner who basically lives with you now. {~There are two toothbrushes and a third pair of shoes.|You've seen them more than the post.|They have opinions about your sofa.}

outcomes.text: The note started a war. The war is ongoing.
They apologized and bought me groceries.
We worked it out like adults.
We talked, they agreed with everything, and then nothing changed at all.
I labeled every item in the fridge. They ate the labels.
I labelled everything, they found it hilarious, and it became the running joke of the flat.

title: Date disaster
text: Your date spent the whole night talking about their ex.
Your date showed up two hours late and brought their mom.

outcomes.text: I faked an emergency. A classic for a reason.
I faked an emergency and ran into them three weeks later, in a very small shop.
It was so bad it became my best story.
I stuck it out and somewhere around the second hour they relaxed and became a different person entirely.

choices.label: Set them up with a friend

outcomes.text: They hit it off. I'm a matchmaker now.
I set them up with a friend and it went badly, and somehow I was blamed by both of them.

title: Wedding invite
text: {f.first} is getting married and wants you there.
You've been invited to {f.first}'s wedding.

outcomes.text: I caught the bouquet. Everyone looked at me.
I gave a speech. People cried. Good crying.
I danced too hard and pulled a hamstring.
I sent something nice from the registry.
I sent a gift instead and heard afterwards that my absence had been noticed and counted.
{f.first} understood. Mostly.
{f.first} said it was fine and did not invite me to anything else for a long time.

title: A stranger in need
text: An elderly man is struggling with heavy grocery bags.
A woman's car won't start in the parking lot. It's raining.
A lost kid is crying at the mall.

outcomes.text: It tripled! $6,000!
It dropped 80%.
I'll never know.
I passed, and watched it climb for a fortnight, and then watched it collapse entirely.

choices.label: Put in what you can lose

outcomes.text: I put in a small amount I could stand to lose, and it did well, and I took the profit and stopped.
I put in what I could lose, and lost it, and that was exactly the deal I had made with myself.

title: A DM from a celebrity
text: {celeb_influencer} just sent you a DM about collaborating.

outcomes.text: We shot a video together. My followers doubled.
It was a scam account pretending to be {celeb_influencer}.

choices.label: Ask what's actually in it for you

outcomes.text: I asked for terms and got them, in writing, and it paid properly.
I asked for terms and they stopped replying within the hour.
I ignored it, and a month later found out it had been genuine, and worth a great deal.
I ignored it, and it turned out to be a scam account that took four other people for thousands.

title: TV kitchen
text: {celeb_chef} is holding open auditions for a cooking show in {city}.

outcomes.text: {celeb_chef} called my risotto "a crime" on live TV. I became a meme.
{celeb_chef} said it was the best dish of the day! I made the final round.
I yelled at the TV the whole time.
I watched at home and fell asleep before the result, and had it spoiled for me at work.
I cooked the one dish I have made a thousand times. They asked for the recipe on camera.
I cooked it under lights, with a clock, and it came out nothing like it does at home.

title: Stadium moment
text: At a game, {celeb_athlete} kicks the ball into the stands, right at you.

outcomes.text: I caught it! {celeb_athlete} signed it after the game.
It hit me in the face. The jumbotron replayed it four times.

choices.label: Give it to the kid behind you

outcomes.text: I turned and handed it to a child who had been screaming for it, and the whole section stood up.
I handed it back and their parent took it off them immediately to sell. I watched it happen.
I sold it that week for more than I earn in a fortnight, and have not regretted it once.
I sold it, and the buyer turned out to be the child I took it from in the first place.

title: Book signing
text: {celeb_author} is signing books at the local bookstore.

outcomes.text: {celeb_author} wrote a long message in mine. I'll keep it forever.
{celeb_author} signed it without looking up, spelled my name wrong, and moved on to the next person.
"Write every day, even when it's bad." I started that night.
I asked for advice and they gave me a considered, specific answer about my own work that I have not stopped thinking about.
They took it, and eleven months later an email arrived with three paragraphs of notes and one introduction.
They took it politely and I watched it go into a bag that was already full of other people's.

title: The billionaire
text: {celeb_tech} is giving a talk in {city} and taking questions.

outcomes.text: {celeb_tech} dodged it, but the clip of my question went viral.
I asked a tough question and my voice went completely. The clip that went round was of that.
{celeb_tech} laughed and said, "Email me." I did. No reply.
{celeb_tech}'s team actually emailed me back.
I said nothing, listened to the whole thing, and left with one idea that changed what I did next.
I said nothing, and afterwards realised everyone who asked something got twenty minutes with them in the lobby.
